newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan to buy bearings from Sweden's SKF.
newsitem.headline: Nissan to buy bearings from Sweden's SKF.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Monday it would start buying wheel bearings from Sweden's AB SKF in September.
Nissan, Japan's second-biggest carmaker, said in a statement that its annual purchases of SKF-made bearings are expected to total about 600 million yen.
The bearings will be used in Nissan's March, Sunny, Pulsar, Bluebird, Primera, Maxima and Cefiro models produced in Japan.

SKF is one of world's major bearing makers, and Nissan's British unit Nissan Motor Manufacturing (UK) Ltd in Sunderland, England, has used its wheel bearings on its Micra model (called the March in Japan) since 1992.
SKF's Airasca plant in Italy will supply the bearings to Nissan.
Last Thursday, SKF said it had signed a contract to supply wheel bearings to Toyota Motor Corp for use in Toyota's Ipsum recreational vehicle, which is known as the Picnic in Europe.
Toyota would not disclose the details of the contract, but a Japanese media report said it called for the purchase of 147 million yen worth of bearings a year.
